messages:
Anya: Heads-up — small-chat endpoints spiked at ~3x p50/p95 right after the 11:41 deploy. Dash shows prefix cache hit-rate collapsed 92% -> 4% and eviction rate shot up. https://internal.metrics/redwood/runtime/graphs/abcd :rotating_light:
ops-bot: ALERT: latency_slo_violations > 5% for /v1/chat (11:42) — routing to @eng-runtime oncall
Mike: looking. any recent config/PRs touching prefix keys or cache?
Ken: I just pulled kernel-selection logs — saw multiple model-worker fallbacks to the slower kernel around the same time (11:41:30+). Memory pressure looks elevated on gpu-2. Not sure if related.
Zoe: I grabbed a quick profile and flamegraph. attaching small snippet:
```\n# memalloc by function (top)\n1. prefix_cache::insert  48%\n2. kv_cache::evict_loop  27%\n3. batching::assign      12%\n4. runtime::kernel_fallback 7%\n```\nZoe: Also noticed a huge number of distinct prefix keys during the incident: cardinality jumped from ~18k to ~420k in 2 minutes.
Ricardo: that screams prefix canonicalization change or key poisoning. Any PRs that changed how we normalize user prompts?
Anya: @Mike — I can repro a bit locally by sending chat requests with slight whitespace variations \"hello\", \"hello \", \"hello\n\" — they end up as different cache keys. We recently merged PR #2148 which adjusted prefix normalization regex to be less aggressive (intent was to preserve trailing whitespace for some flows).
Mike: oh. timeline matches. batching heuristic change was also merged in the same deploy — it increased batch window slightly which increased per-worker KV entries in-flight. Combined could push us over memory threshold and trigger aggressive evictions.
Ken: kernel fallback log excerpt:
```\n[11:41:35] kernel_selector: selected kernel=fast_attn_v2\n[11:41:36] kernel_selector: fallback to safe_attn_int8 due to OOM\n[11:41:36] worker: kv_cache_evict triggered, freed=48MB\n```\nKen: so fallback => smaller kernel memory footprints wrong, actually fallback caused higher memory churn because int8 kernel path allocs awkwardly with KV caches. Strange but observable.
Zoe: root cause hypothesis: PR #2148 loosened prefix canonicalization -> key explosion -> higher unique entries per worker -> batching window bump kept more distinct prefixes live -> cache hit-rate collapse -> eviction loop -> kernel fallback + more evictions => latency spike.
Ricardo: agreed. quick mitigation options:
- rollback prefix normalization change (fast)
- revert batching window tweak (fast if rollback safe)
- increase cache limit (hotfix, risky for OOM)
- add TTL to new prefix namespace (short-term)

Anya: I pushed a rollback for PR #2148 to the canary cluster and throttled the batch window to previous value on canary.
ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: rollback-pr-2148 deployed to canary (11:52) by Anya
Zoe: canary metrics already improving — prefix cardinality dropping, hit-rate back to ~88% after ~90s.
Mike: rolling the rollback to prod now.
ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: rollback-pr-2148 deployed to prod (12:04) by Mike
Ricardo: prod hit-rate trending back up, p50/p95 back to normal baselines. Eviction rate down.
Anya: incident postmortem action items:
- add unit tests for prefix canonicalization and rounding whitespace rules (owner: Anya)
- add an alert when prefix cardinality spikes > 3x baseline for 1m (owner: Ken)
- add eviction-loop detection + early TTL fallback (owner: Ricardo)
- evaluate kernel-selection memory heuristics for int8 fallback corner-case (owner: Zoe)
- track batching window changes with perf gating (owner: Mike)
Mike: I'll open follow-up PRs for perf gating and a canary check that runs synthetic traffic with prefix variants.
Ken: also adding a quick profiler that dumps top mem alloc callers when eviction rate > threshold.
Anya: thanks everyone. Filing short incident report and linking to this thread. :thumbsup:
Zoe: postmortem note — weird interaction between two independent changes (prefix normalization + batching tweak). reminds us to run higher-cardinality synthetic tests on canary before deploy.
Ricardo: closing incident in 2h after watch window if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
